leads.found_by: phase1a smoke-test answerer (sonnet, magpie-helper, arena real arm)
leads.claim: "MAgPIE's spatial resolution is configurable via `cfg$magpie_folder` and the input data"
leads.finder_said: cfg$magpie_folder does not appear in config/default.cfg; looks fabricated or confused
leads.my_rederivation: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, and the finder OVERSTATED it. `magpie_folder` appears 0x in config/default.cfg but DOES exist in the model repo: scripts/start_functions.R and scripts/run_submit/submit.R. So it is a real object (the repo path), not a phantom identifier. The defect is a MIS-ATTRIBUTED MECHANISM: resolution is set by which pre-clustered cellular input `cfg$input["cellular"]` points at (config/default.cfg:26, resolution encoded in the filename as _c200_), not by cfg$magpie_folder.
leads.gate_visible: unknown - check_fenced_identifiers only binds tokens carrying a MAgPIE type/module prefix, and `cfg$magpie_folder` carries none, so probably blind (same coverage hole as the ssp_scenario phantom)
leads.why_it_matters: notes files are ALWAYS read when answering about their module (AGENT.md Step 1), so a wrong lever here propagates directly to users.

leads.found_by: phase1a smoke-test answerer (sonnet, magpie-helper, arena real arm)
leads.claim: Number of 0.5-degree land grid cells is given as 67,420 in one set of docs and 59,199 in another.
leads.finder_said: flagged as an unresolved numeric inconsistency rather than picking one
leads.my_rederivation: CONFIRMED AS AN INCONSISTENCY, NOT YET RESOLVED. Both numbers verified present at the cited lines. Which is correct is NOT established - it needs the actual land mask / LPJmL cell list, which I have not read. Do not repair by picking the more common number.
leads.gate_visible: no - check_intra_doc_contradiction operates within a doc; this contradiction spans core_docs/ and modules/
leads.why_it_matters: a cross-file numeric contradiction is a checkable class the battery currently cannot see; if common, it argues for a cross-file numeric-consistency checker rather than more audits.
